papers.title: Strategic repositioning of focal firms in business ecosystems: a trajectory-based perspective
papers.abstract: Purpose This study examines how focal firms evolve within business ecosystems over time. While prior research has explored ecosystem strategies, structural changes, and firm-level adaptations, it has often examined these dynamics either through specific dimensions or within a limited set of cases. The purpose of this study is to identify and systematically organize the distinct trajectories through which focal firms reposition within ecosystems, and explain the conditions under which different trajectories emerge. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a comparative multiple-case design based on longitudinal secondary data across diverse industries. Using a theoretically informed yet inductive approach, focal firms were analyzed over extended time horizons to identify recurring patterns of strategic repositioning. Findings The analysis identifies five strategic trajectories through which focal firms reposition by reconfiguring the locus of complementarity (internal vs. external) and market scope (current vs. new). The findings show that focal firm evolution is not uniform or stage-based but follows patterned trajectories shaped by technological pressures, architectural constraints, and firm-level capabilities. Importantly, firm evolution does not necessarily require transformation across architectural positions; deliberately reinforcing an existing configuration can also constitute a coherent and high-performing strategy. Originality/value This study contributes to ecosystem research by developing an integrative conceptual framework that identifies and compares multiple trajectories of firm evolution. By moving beyond fragmented, dimension-specific analyses, it offers a structured and process-oriented understanding of ecosystem transformation.
papers.summary_ja: ビジネスエコシステム内でフォーカル企業が戦略的な位置づけを変えていく際の5つの軌跡パターンを識別し、プロセス指向のエコシステム変革フレームワークを提示する。既存ポジションの意図的強化も有効戦略として認識される。

papers.title: Understanding Sustainable Business Model Barriers: The Interplay of Sustainable Value Dynamics and Organizational Tensions
papers.abstract: Sustainability-oriented startups face challenges in implementing sustainable business models due to resource constraints, technological uncertainty and competing economic, social and environmental objectives. Although prior studies have identified numerous sustainable business model barriers, limited attention has been given to the organizational dynamics underlying their emergence. Drawing on paradox theory, this study explores the relationship between sustainable value dynamics, organizational tensions and perception of sustainable business model barriers. A structured brainstorming tool, the Mix-Tool, was developed and applied in five sustainability-oriented startups, and the resulting qualitative data were analysed through coding techniques. The findings suggest that sustainable value misalignment dynamics, together with organizational tensions, support a deeper understanding of perceived barriers. These misalignments arise from discrepancies between proposed, created, expected, perceived, measured, captured, uncaptured and potential value across business-, work-, offering- and cascaded system-related dimensions. The study discusses implications for coping strategies, including acceptance, separation and synthesis.

papers.title: The refined interaction value framework: advancing value co-creation in human–AI service systems in the AI-era
papers.abstract: This paper aims to advance understanding of value co-creation and co-destruction in artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled services by introducing the Refined Interaction Value Framework (R-IVF). The R-IVF explains how interaction value depends not only on technical performance, but also on how users interpret machine initiative, calibrate trust, experience meaningful exploration and evaluate contextual fit. This paper develops R-IVF conceptually by integrating three AI-era constructs – Agentic Perception (AP), Dynamic Trust Calibration (DTC) and Serendipitous Exploration (SE) – into the original framework and reconceptualizing Value Configuration as Contextual Intelligence. The paper shows that interaction value in AI-enabled service is shaped by three recurrent tensions: increasing machine agency within interaction, need for dynamically calibrated trust and challenge of preserving meaningful exploration under increasingly personalized service conditions. These tensions may either support value co-creation or contribute to value co-destruction.
papers.summary_ja: AIサービスにおける価値共創・共破壊のメカニズムを、Agentic Perception・Dynamic Trust Calibration・Serendipitous Explorationの3新概念でアップデートした精緻化相互作用価値フレームワーク（R-IVF）を提案する。

papers.title: From diagnosis to design: a hybrid human–LLM framework integrating fsQCA and TRIZ for cultural service innovation
papers.abstract: Digital cultural services, such as museum virtual exhibitions, must create meaningful visitor experiences. However, design teams often face complex combinations of user, technological, and experiential factors. This study aims to develop a structured Human-AI collaborative framework that converts configurational insights into service innovation concepts for digital museum exhibitions. It introduces a novel Hybrid Human-LLM framework that integrates fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), TRIZ inventive principles, and Large Language Models (LLMs) with Human-in-the-Loop validation design. The four-stage process begins with fsQCA identifying configurational pathways to high perceived visitor impact. LLM-assisted reasoning then translates configurations into TRIZ technical contradictions, followed by TRIZ-based concept generation. Finally, expert evaluation validates the proposed designs.
papers.summary_ja: デジタル文化施設のサービス革新において、fsQCAで体験条件を診断しLLMとTRIZで設計解を生成するHuman-in-the-Loop型ハイブリッドフレームワークを提案・検証する。

papers.title: What makes an effective ideator? The distinct roles of cognition, personality, and experience in early-stage venture ideation
papers.abstract: A microfoundational account of organizational innovation capability should explain which individual-level attributes distinguish ideators who are better able to generate, select, and elaborate ideas into investment-worthy business concepts. Drawing on Trait Activation Theory, we conceptualize venture ideation as a staged, trait-relevant context in which cognitive abilities, personality traits, and domain creative experience are differentially expressed across successive stages. We examine this theorizing using a task-based assessment with innovation-exposed experts including R&D managers and entrepreneurs (n=208). Divergent thinking predicted idea quantity, but not investor-evaluated idea quality. Investment-interest judgments were predicted by ideators' Openness to Experience, domain creative experience, and convergent thinking ability. Our findings show that early-stage venture ideation is not a unitary creative process.
papers.summary_ja: R&Dマネージャー・起業家208名の実験から、発散的思考はアイデア量を予測するが投資価値のある概念精緻化には経験・収束的思考・開放性が鍵であることを示す。

papers.title: Beyond Problem-Solving: The Social Management System as the Subject of Public Policy
papers.abstract: Public policy analysis has long been organized around the idea that governing consists in defining and solving public problems. Yet decades of debate on problem definition, framing and wicked problems have shown that problems are unstable, contested and rarely amenable to definitive solutions. Drawing on social systems theory as a theoretical frame of reference, I contend that policy objects of intervention are decision-oriented constructions that make complex situations governable. Because policy cannot act directly upon social systems, it operates instead on the social management system: the emergent pattern of interdependent management decisions through which societies collectively respond to publicly problematized situations. Public policy is thus reconceptualized as a second-order form of social governance that reorients management rather than solving substantive social problems.
papers.summary_ja: 公共政策は「社会問題を解く」のではなく「社会マネジメントシステムを方向づける」という、社会システム理論を用いた政策介入の存在論的再定義を提示する。

papers.title: Beyond the Departure Gate: De-Anchoring Tourism Through Strategic Foresight
papers.abstract: Tourism scholarship has long treated technological innovation as an accelerant bolted onto a stable practice: people move through physical space to consume experiences, then return home. This conceptual paper asks what happens to the field's theory once that assumption is relaxed. Rather than forecasting a single future, it develops a structured conceptual foresight framework to examine how emerging technological trajectories may challenge the constitutive assumptions of tourism theory. Drawing on tourism scholarship alongside developments in computation, biosciences, and cognitive science, the framework integrates established concepts from futures studies including Voros's futures cone, Inayatullah's causal layered analysis, and Dator's four generic futures to explore alternative trajectories for tourism. The analysis identifies four constitutive assumptions of tourism theory and develops a typology of de-anchoring. Four conceptual scenarios follow: dematerialization of place, biologically mediated travel, autonomous destination ecosystems, and erosion of the tourist-host distinction.
papers.summary_ja: 観光論の4つの構成的前提を未来技術の観点で「脱アンカー」し、代替シナリオを展開するフォーサイトフレームワーク。前提を問い直すデザイン思考の方法論として他領域に転用可能。

papers.title: Are circular innovations disruptive? An analysis of the role of inventor networks in the European semiconductor industry
papers.abstract: The expansion of advanced technologies is intensifying demand for energy, materials, and efficiency of production systems, with semiconductors exemplifying the tension between rapid technological progress and resource sustainability, and the development of circular innovations. The empirical analysis relies on patents of 299 European Semiconductor Equipment Manufacturing (SEM) companies retrieved from the ORBIS IP database for the period 2013-2022. Our findings show that circular innovations exhibit, on average, higher disruptiveness than non-circular patents, and that inventor network structures characterized by more peripheral and high local cohesive configurations align with circular disruptive outcomes. The effect of the antecedents differs systematically between circular and non-circular innovations, indicating distinct pathways to disruption. The study contributes to innovation literature by integrating a structural measure of disruptiveness, offering one of the first patent-level comparisons of circular versus non-circular innovations in the semiconductor industry.
